claim: QS-23 says every create beyond ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR within an hour is refused, and the deployment view says to run any number of replicas behind one URL. evidence: Document, docs/arc42/README.md:254: "Where `ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR` is set, each create beyond it within an hour is refused, naming the limit; nothing is inserted"; docs/arc42/README.md:176: "Enterich is one stateless container: no volume, no database. Any number of replicas behind one URL." Code, src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:61-65: `# A lock per DocType, held by a create from its count of drafts per hour to its insert` `creating: defaultdict[str, anyio.Lock]`, which lives in each process's Context; src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:119: `async with context.creating[doctype]:`. verdict.reproduction: Document: docs/arc42/README.md:254 (QS-23): "Where `ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR` is set, each create beyond it within an hour is refused, naming the limit; nothing is inserted". docs/arc42/README.md:176: "Enterich is one stateless container: no volume, no database. So the diagram reads the template only after the duplicate check, and only when the create goes ahead. Code, src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:264-276: `if inputs.taxes_and_charges is not None: taxes = await drafts.tax_rows(context, SALES.template, inputs.taxes_and_charges)` runs before `matches = await drafts.duplicates(...)` and `if matches and not inputs.allow_duplicate: raise drafts.refuse_duplicates(matches, DRAFT_MATCH)`. src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:60-65: `tax_rows` first calls `get_named(..., field="taxes_and_charges", what="the tax template", company=True)` (frappe.client.get), then `context.erpnext.tax_rows(doctype, template)` (get_taxes_and_charges). src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:336-354 (create_draft_purchase_invoice) uses the same order: tax_rows before the duplicate check. location: docs/arc42/README.md:6. Runtime view / Updating a draft
claim: The architecture says Enterich learns the agent user's name at the first update, and that renaming the agent user only makes Enterich refuse the agent's own drafts until a restart. The code also asks for the name at the first create counted against ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR, and it filters that hourly count on the cached name. So after a rename the count finds nothing, and the drafts-per-hour limit stops working until a restart.
evidence: Document, docs/arc42/README.md:172: "Enterich learns the agent user's name at the first update, from `frappe.auth.get_logged_user`, and keeps it until it stops ... Renaming the agent user in ERPNext needs a restart; until then Enterich refuses the agent's own drafts as another user's." Code, src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:119-125 (insert, used by every create when the limit is set): `async with context.creating[doctype]: made = await context.erpnext.get_list(... ["owner", "=", await context.erpnext.user()], ["creation", ">", ago(...)]` ...)`. src/enterich/erpnext.py:127-131: `if self._user is None: ... self._user = _expect(answer, "message", str)`, which is asked once and then kept. REQ-001 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:608) says the same as the code: "`frappe.auth.get_logged_user` for the agent user's name, at the first update or counted create". Frappe's User.after_rename (frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py:732-743 on the end-to-end site) runs `UPDATE ... SET owner = new WHERE owner = old` on every table, so the drafts the agent made in the last hour then carry the new name, and the count filtered on the old one returns none.
proposal: Change the sentences to: "Enterich learns the agent user's name at the first update, or at the first create when ENTERICH_MAX_DRAFTS_PER_HOUR is set, from `frappe.auth.get_logged_user`, and keeps it until it stops ... Renaming the agent user in ERPNext needs a restart: until then Enterich refuses the agent's own drafts as another user's, and the limit of drafts per hour counts none of the agent's drafts, so it does not limit anything."

verdict.reproduction: Document, docs/arc42/README.md:172: "Enterich learns the agent user's name at the first update, from `frappe.auth.get_logged_user`, and keeps it until it stops ... Renaming the agent user in ERPNext needs a restart; until then Enterich refuses the agent's own drafts as another user's." Code, src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:118-127 (insert, when max_drafts_per_hour is set): `async with context.creating[doctype]: made = await context.erpnext.get_list(doctype, ..., filters=[["company", "=", ...], ["owner", "=", await context.erpnext.user()], ["creation", ">", ago(...)]], ...)` then `if len(made) >= limit: raise Refusal(...)`. src/enterich/erpnext.py:127-132: `async def user(self): if self._user is None: answer = await self._call("GET", f"/api/method/{LOGGED_USER_METHOD}", {}); self._user = _expect(answer, "message", str); return self._user` — asked once, kept. Spec agrees with the code: docs/specs/req-001-core.md (ERPNext calls) "`frappe.auth.get_logged_user` for the agent user's name, at the first update or counted create ... a list of the agent user's documents of the DocType created since an hour ago (`owner`, `creation`) for the limit of REQ-001-PRS-F019". Frappe's User.after_rename (frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py:727-738 in the local bench copy) runs `UPDATE <tab> SET owner = new WHERE owner = old` on every table, so after a rename the count filtered on the cached old name finds none of the agent's drafts and the per-hour limit never refuses until a restart. Read from source; nothing run.
verdict.reason: The code matches REQ-001 (name fetched at the first update or counted create, cached; hourly count filtered on owner = cached name), so the document is the wrong side. docs/arc42/README.md:172 names only the first update as when the name is learnt, and gives refusing the agent's own drafts as the only effect of a rename. It leaves out that the drafts-per-hour limit stops counting, which is a weakened limit and not just wording. No other sentence of the arc42 document covers this. Neither the backlog nor tests/repo mention a rename. docs/arc42/README.md is a document the pipeline may correct, so the class is fix and no test file is needed.

claim: The description says that what isn't allocated becomes an advance, named in `warnings`. The code warns only when the draft has references. A payment created without `references` is booked entirely as an advance and gets no warning.
evidence: Description: "Allocate the payment to the party's submitted, open invoices with `references`, ...; what isn't allocated becomes an advance, named in `warnings`." (src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:662-665). Code: "if rows_of(saved, \"references\") and unallocated > 0: warnings.append(...)" (bank_and_cash.py:447). Spec DoD: "one fully allocated, and one without references, returns none" (docs/specs/req-007-bank-and-cash.md, REQ-007-PRS-F007).
proposal: Reword to: "...; when `references` leave part of `paid_amount` unallocated, that part becomes an advance and `warnings` names it. Without `references` the whole payment is an advance, without a warning."

verdict.reproduction: Document: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:662-665 (create_draft_payment_entry description) says "Allocate the payment to the party's submitted, open invoices with `references`, each at most its outstanding amount and together at most `paid_amount`; what isn't allocated becomes an advance, named in `warnings`." Since `references` is optional, a reader takes a payment without references as wholly unallocated and expects a warning. Code: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:447 `if rows_of(saved, "references") and unallocated > 0:` is the only place the advance warning is added, so a draft without references gets no advance warning. Spec: docs/specs/req-007-bank-and-cash.md:142 says to warn only "when the draft has references and part of its paid amount isn't allocated", and :149 says "one fully allocated, and one without references, returns none". The code matches the spec. The description is the side that is wrong.
verdict.reason: The code (bank_and_cash.py:447) follows REQ-007-PRS-F007 (req-007-bank-and-cash.md:142, :149): the advance warning is added only when the draft has references. The tool description (bank_and_cash.py:662-665) says without condition that what isn't allocated is named in `warnings`. That would include a payment without references, which never gets the warning, so the document is the wrong side, as the finding says. No other sentence in the description adds the condition. docs/backlog/backlog.md has no entry for this, and nothing in tests/repo/ compares the description with this behaviour. The spec does not word the tool's description, so the pipeline may reword it (class: fix, no test file). None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: The get_item description promises "the accounts and cost centres the assigned company uses for it". The code returns only the fields of the item's own Item Default row for the company, and null when that row or a field in it is empty. In that case ERPNext still books to the item group's or the company's default account, so a null does not mean the company uses no account for the item.
evidence: Description: "Get one item by its exact item code, with the accounts and cost centres the assigned company uses for it and its item tax templates." (src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:100-101). Code: "defaults = next((r for r in rows_of(doc, \"item_defaults\") if r.get(\"company\") == company), None)" and "**{field: defaults and defaults.get(field) for field in DEFAULT_FIELDS}" (master_data.py:64, 70). The spec calls them the item's Item Default row: "`get_item` SHALL return only the assigned company's Item Default row" (docs/specs/req-003-master-data.md, REQ-003-PRS-F001).
proposal: Change the description to: "Get one item by its exact item code, with its defaults for the assigned company (`income_account`, `expense_account`, `selling_cost_center`, `buying_cost_center`) and its item tax templates. An empty default means the item sets none: ERPNext then takes the item group's or the company's, so leave the row's account out rather than pick one."

verdict.reproduction: Document: src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:100-101 says get_item returns "the accounts and cost centres the assigned company uses for it". Code: src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:64 `defaults = next((r for r in rows_of(doc, "item_defaults") if r.get("company") == company), None)` and :70 `**{field: defaults and defaults.get(field) for field in DEFAULT_FIELDS}`. So each of income_account, expense_account, selling_cost_center and buying_cost_center comes only from the item's own Item Default row for the company. When that row is missing, the result is None, and when one of its fields is empty, the result is that empty value. Item group, brand and company defaults are never looked at. ERPNext uses the item group's or the company's default when the item sets none, so the description promises more than the code delivers. Static reading only; nothing was run.
verdict.reason: The code matches the spec: REQ-003-PRS-F001 at docs/specs/req-003-master-data.md:42 and its catalogue at :59/:65 say the values come from the item's Item Default row for the assigned company. The wrong side is the tool description at src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:100-101, so "document" is the right side to fix. The spec catalogue gives fields, not description wording, so the pipeline may correct the description. A reader of the description would take a null income_account to mean the company books no account for this item. In ERPNext, though, the account then comes from the item group or the company default. That is a wrong promise, not just wording. No other sentence of the description qualifies it. The open backlog items in docs/backlog/backlog.md don't cover it; the only item touching this area is item_tax_template per line, which is a different gap. No check in tests/repo compares tool description wording with these semantics. None of the three patterns fits. The proposed rewording works; if the fix stage wants it shorter, it could leave out the instruction to leave the row's account out. That sentence is advice, but it is consistent with create_draft_sales_invoice taking an optional income_account (src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:153).

claim: The descriptions of create_draft_purchase_invoice and create_draft_sales_invoice say `posting_date` defaults to today, but when it is left out the code sends no posting date and no `set_posting_time`. The draft's posting date is therefore never fixed: ERPNext sets it again to the day of each later save, so an update on a later day moves the posting date (and with it the due date).
evidence: Description: "`posting_date` defaults to today, `due_date` to the supplier's payment terms" (src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:568-569); same in the sales description: "`posting_date` defaults to today, `due_date` to the customer's payment terms" (src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:430-431). Code sends the date only when given: "if inputs.posting_date is not None: doc |= {\"posting_date\": ..., \"set_posting_time\": 1}" (procure_to_pay.py:291-292, order_to_cash.py:258-259). Compare the returns, which send it either way: "posting_date = inputs.posting_date or today(...)" with "set_posting_time": 1 (procure_to_pay.py:424-429). drafts.py:198-199: "# A draft without a fixed posting date gets today's at this save. moves = not stored.get(\"set_posting_time\") and stored.get(\"posting_date\") != str(day)". The test tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:1095-1113 (test_a_floating_draft_can_be_updated_on_a_later_day) shows a draft posted yesterday and then updated with only `remarks` coming back with posting_date and due_date TODAY.
proposal: In both invoice create descriptions, replace "`posting_date` defaults to today" with: "Without `posting_date` the draft has no fixed posting date: ERPNext gives it the day of each save, so a later update moves it, and its due date with it. Give `posting_date` to fix it, for instance the date the bill is to be booked on."

verdict.reproduction: Document: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:568-569 says "`posting_date` defaults to today, `due_date` to the supplier's payment terms", and src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:430-431 says "`posting_date` defaults to today, `due_date` to the customer's payment terms". Neither description, nor the input fields (procure_to_pay.py:183, order_to_cash.py:162, both plain `posting_date: Day | None = None`), says the date is not fixed. Code: procure_to_pay.py:291-292 sends `posting_date` and `set_posting_time: 1` only when `posting_date` is given (order_to_cash.py:258-259 does the same), so a draft created without it is saved with set_posting_time 0. drafts.py:198-199: "# A draft without a fixed posting date gets today's at this save. moves = not stored.get(\"set_posting_time\") and stored.get(\"posting_date\") != str(day)", and that clears the payment schedule and due date so they are counted again. tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:1095-1113 (test_a_floating_draft_can_be_updated_on_a_later_day) shows a draft dated yesterday, updated with only `remarks`, coming back with posting_date and due_date set to TODAY. The specs record the same ERPNext behaviour: docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md:243 and docs/specs/req-005-procure-to-pay.md:266 say "An invoice saved with `set_posting_time` 0 gets today ... as posting date at every save". Compare the returns and journal entries, where the catalogue says "(default today, sent either way)" (req-004:193, req-006:190) and the code sends the date (procure_to_pay.py:348). verdict.reason:
The finding holds. The two invoice create descriptions say `posting_date` "defaults to today". Code and specs both show something different: without the input, no posting date or set_posting_time is sent, so the date is not fixed. ERPNext gives the draft today's date on every save, so an update made through the tool on a later day moves the posting date and the due date (drafts.py:198-201, test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:1095-1113). A client reading "defaults to today" would expect the date to stay as created.

The code is not the wrong side. The specs mean the date to float: the catalogue says "(default today)" for invoices (req-004:183, req-005:203) but "(default today, sent either way)" for returns and journal entries. Their ERPNext facts (req-004:243, req-005:266) describe the date moving. So the document is what's wrong.

It is not just wording, because the moving due date is left out. No other sentence in either description covers it. Neither the update descriptions nor the input fields mention it. docs/backlog/backlog.md has nothing on posting dates. The only check in tests/repo/ that reads descriptions is test_server_json.py, and it does not compare this behaviour.

Classed as fix: the description is tool text in src/enterich/tools/, not wording the spec dictates. The proposed sentence only adds what req-004:243 and req-005:266 already state, and it stays consistent with the catalogue's "(default today)", since a create does get today's date. No spec change is needed. The document is wrong, so there are no test files.
